category: process identity and destructive lifecycle control
title: A reused PID is accepted when only the working directory matches, allowing an unrelated process tree to be killed
observed_behavior: active_job_pid_matches_record treats the command-line and cwd checks as alternatives: any True result proves identity even when the other inspectable result is False. A synthetic current-code probe used a stale validate-only record for pwsh and a live notepad process with the same cwd; the verdict was True. cleanup_stale_validate_active_jobs then obtains that PID and kills its process tree.
expected_invariant: A destructive stale-process cleanup must require a non-contradictory exact launch identity. A reused PID with an inspectable command line that contradicts the ActiveJobs record must never be treated as the recorded process, even when its cwd happens to match.
root_cause: The identity reducer uses any(True) before checking for contradictory False results and records neither process creation time nor another immutable process identity.
failure_scenario: A validate-only backend dies and its PID is reused by an unrelated process launched from the same repository or application directory. After the heartbeat threshold, cleanup classifies the unrelated process as the old launch and terminates it and its children.
evidence: Current lines 249-258 return True when either cwd or cmdline matches.
Current lines 417-424 pass the accepted psutil process directly to kill_psutil_process_tree.
The isolated bundled-Python probe returned {'same_cwd_different_cmdline_verdict': True}.
Existing reused-PID coverage tests only a case where both cwd and command line differ.
existing_safeguards: PID liveness and zombie checks
cwd and command-line inspection
ambiguous inspection fails closed
cleanup is limited to stale validate-only records
safeguard_gap: The reducer lets a weak cwd match override a positive command-line contradiction, and the resulting verdict authorizes a destructive kill.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_process_active_jobs.py covers dead PIDs, both-fields mismatch, inspection denial, and normal validate-only cleanup
tests_missing: Same cwd plus contradictory command line must return False
PID creation-time mismatch
cleanup must not kill a reused unrelated PID
recommended_remediation: Bind ActiveJobs to process creation time when launching and require it on cleanup. At minimum, treat any inspectable contradiction as False and require every available strong identity field to agree before killing.
remediation_risk: medium: stricter identity checks can leave genuinely stale validate-only work blocking when process metadata is inaccessible; preserve the existing fail-closed operator path
validation_rung: Focused ActiveJobs identity and stale-cleanup unit tests with fake processes, process-lifecycle/close-readiness tests, and a disposable real-process PID identity probe; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit finding; no existing finding fragment matched the PID-identity reducer or same-cwd contradiction.

title: Durable lifecycle leases use PID liveness without launch identity and can remain falsely active after PID reuse
observed_behavior: Lease state records owner_pid/child_pid but no process creation time, command identity, executable, or cwd. status and stale-recovery admission classify the lease solely by whether that integer PID currently exists. A dead MediaPipeline PID reused by any process is therefore reported active and is ineligible for automatic or operator reconciliation.
expected_invariant: Restart recovery must distinguish the exact lease owner/child from an unrelated later process with the same PID, while ambiguous evidence remains fail closed and actionable.
root_cause: Lifecycle lease identity is represented only by an OS-recyclable PID and the liveness callback accepts no durable launch fingerprint.
failure_scenario: The backend or child dies, its PID is reused by a long-running unrelated process, and the next backend sees the interrupted lease as active. New work, close readiness, automatic recovery, and retire-without-replay remain blocked until the unrelated process exits or state is manually altered.
evidence: Lease payload lines 191-203 stores PIDs but no creation-time identity.
status lines 250-256 maps pid_alive=True directly to active.
begin_one_recovery_attempt and retire_stale_without_replay both require pid_alive is exactly False.
Existing ActiveJobs code already demonstrates that PID liveness alone is insufficient and has separate identity inspection.
existing_safeguards: Exclusive lock file
durable lease/recovery/indeterminate records
unknown liveness fails closed
one-shot recovery limit
safeguard_gap: Fail-closed behavior is safe for media but has no truthful or bounded recovery route when a recycled PID is conclusively not the recorded launch.
tests_present: Lifecycle lease/reconciliation tests cover live, dead, unknown, and one-shot recovery postures using injected liveness
tests_missing: Reused PID with mismatched process creation time or command identity
operator recovery from a provably unrelated live PID
recommended_remediation: Persist a process creation-time/executable or other immutable launch token in the lease, verify it alongside PID liveness, and classify an identity mismatch as stale while preserving unknown as blocking.
remediation_risk: medium-high: false stale classification could replay active media work; identity evidence and migration of old leases must be fail closed
validation_rung: Lifecycle lease/recovery unit tests for PID reuse and legacy records, close-readiness tests, and disposable process restart probes; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit reliability finding; no existing lease-identity finding was present.

title: Queue source inventory silently skips directory traversal errors and reports inventory_complete
observed_behavior: The scanner wraps iteration in try/except OSError but calls os.walk without onerror. os.walk handles descendant scandir failures internally and silently skips them when onerror is None, so the outer except does not receive those failures. The result still sets status=inventory_complete and emits no warning for inaccessible subtrees.
expected_invariant: Read-only discovery may continue after inaccessible paths, but its evidence must explicitly distinguish complete from partial enumeration and surface every traversal failure that can undercount media/sidecar inventory.
root_cause: The implementation assumes os.walk propagates descendant errors to the surrounding try block instead of using its onerror callback.
failure_scenario: A configured library contains a permission-denied or transiently unavailable subtree. Fast inventory and library aggregate counts omit its media and sidecars while the status says completed; operators cannot distinguish an empty subtree from an unreadable one.
evidence: os.walk is constructed at line 185 without onerror.
Warnings are appended only for root prechecks, row stat failures, the ineffective outer iteration catch, and row-limit truncation.
Returned status at line 241 is unconditionally inventory_complete.
Existing source-scan tests cover ordinary candidates, sidecars, and launchability but not an inaccessible descendant.
existing_safeguards: Missing/non-directory roots warn
individual candidate stat failures are skipped
inventory rows are explicitly non-launchable
authoritative queue curation follows in the normal combined mode
safeguard_gap: Authoritative curation does not repair the truthfulness of the separately persisted fast inventory or inventory_only mode.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_queue_source_scan.py covers ordinary discovery, sidecars, duplicate scan serialization, and curation status
tests_missing: os.walk descendant onerror produces partial/error evidence
inventory_only mode cannot report complete after a traversal failure
recommended_remediation: Pass an onerror callback that records path/error evidence, track partial completion explicitly, and propagate it into queue scan status and library summaries.
remediation_risk: low-medium: network filesystems can emit many transient errors; bound/deduplicate warnings without converting partial scans into false success
validation_rung: Temporary-tree queue source-scan tests with injected os.walk errors plus library-summary/API status tests; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit finding; no matching source-inventory traversal finding was present.

title: Idle runs surface stale FFmpeg log fields as loaded current progress
observed_behavior: ffmpeg_progress_payload appends a parsed row whenever the bounded log tail contains recognized key/value fields, before checking whether pipeline/worker evidence is active. The now argument is discarded. A current-code probe with Status=Idle, a January timestamp, and an old progress=end block returned status=loaded and one row.

root_cause: Parsed fields are treated as sufficient liveness evidence, and no timestamp freshness or terminal progress marker is applied to the primary fields branch.
failure_scenario: After encoding completes or the backend restarts, the log tail still ends in FFmpeg fields. Diagnostics shows a loaded FFmpeg row for an idle run, misleading the operator about active work and performance.
evidence: lines 271-275 append fields unconditionally; activity is checked only in the no-fields branch.
line 268 explicitly ignores now.
The synthetic exact-code probe returned status loaded, row_count 1 for Idle progress dated 2026-01-01.
The idle unit test uses an empty log and therefore misses stale-field residue.
existing_safeguards: No row is synthesized for idle progress when the log has no parsed fields

safeguard_gap: Neither safeguard correlates parsed log fields to an active job/run or bounds their age.

tests_missing: Idle plus old parsed fields is idle/historical

timestamp/ActiveJobs correlation
recommended_remediation: Require active correlated pipeline/worker evidence for a current row, parse terminal markers, use now to enforce freshness, and expose historical evidence under an explicitly non-current status if retained.

title: Unreadable local-worker claim state is replaced with an empty store and duplicate source claims are admitted
observed_behavior: Get-MediaPipelineLocalWorkerClaimStore catches every read/JSON error and returns a fresh empty claim store. Subsequent claim operations run under the mutex but make their duplicate decision against that empty state, so corruption or read denial erases active ownership evidence.
expected_invariant: The authoritative local-worker claim ledger must fail closed when an existing store cannot be read and validated; synchronization around an untrusted empty substitute must never authorize duplicate work.
root_cause: Missing state and unreadable/corrupt existing state share the same fallback path, and schema/claims shape is normalized without a trust verdict.
failure_scenario: One worker actively owns a source while the claim JSON is partially written, corrupted, or temporarily unreadable. A second worker loads an empty substitute and successfully claims the same source, causing concurrent remux/encode/publish attempts.
evidence: line 97 swallows the complete exception and sets store to null; line 98 returns a new empty store.
The mutex serializes claim mutation but cannot recover evidence discarded before the decision.
Existing local-worker tests cover valid duplicate claims and lifecycle repair but no malformed/unreadable claim store.
Exact PowerShell parser pass found zero syntax errors; this is semantic fail-open behavior.
existing_safeguards: Cross-process mutex
active-status filtering
PID/start-time reconciliation for readable claims
atomic claim-store writes
safeguard_gap: Atomic writes reduce corruption probability but read failure is explicitly converted into empty authority, defeating every higher-level duplicate check.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-LocalWorkerSlotChecks.ps1 covers capacity, valid duplicates, process identity, and repair
tests_missing: Malformed JSON blocks claims
access-denied/read failure blocks claims
unknown schema/root/claims shape fails closed
recommended_remediation: Distinguish missing from existing-unreadable state, strictly validate schema/claims, throw a stable blocking error on untrusted existing state, and provide an explicit evidence-preserving repair/reconciliation path.
remediation_risk: medium-high: fail-closed state can pause workers after transient storage failures; recovery must not discard live claims
validation_rung: PowerShell claim-store unit tests with temporary malformed and injected read-failure fixtures, local-worker concurrency tests, and duplicate-source lifecycle smoke; real media is not required.

observed_behavior: When Get-ChildItem of the pending root fails, the function logs a warning but retains an empty manifest array. It then computes count=0, no age/retry evidence, and Blocked=False, allowing queue orchestration to continue as if no parked outputs existed.

failure_scenario: A permission, network, or filesystem error hides parked manifests. The engine admits new work despite configured backlog/age/retry backpressure, increasing duplicate output and storage pressure while telemetry claims zero manifests.

lines 64-79 derive every block condition from the empty list.
the returned object has no scan_error/read_health field.

title: Phase planning reloads the priority manifest without fail-closed semantics after discovery validated it
observed_behavior: Queue discovery loads the priority manifest with -FailClosed and annotates entries, but phase planning separately calls Get-PriorityManifest without -FailClosed for manual/deadline sorting. If the manifest becomes corrupt or unreadable between those reads, the sorting layer falls back while previously annotated levels remain, silently losing manual positions/deadlines.
expected_invariant: A single queue plan must use one trusted priority-manifest snapshot, or every re-read must fail closed and be fingerprint-correlated; operator ordering must not degrade mid-plan.
root_cause: Priority data is re-read at the phase boundary instead of passing the already validated immutable manifest/metadata through the plan.
failure_scenario: An operator save or filesystem failure races discovery and sorting. Hold/high/low buckets reflect the first manifest, but manual/deadline order uses an empty fallback from the second read, producing an order not represented by either coherent manifest version.
evidence: queue_entries.ps1 lines 266-269 calls Get-PriorityManifest -FailClosed.
phase_plan.ps1 line 143 calls Get-PriorityManifest without the switch.
priority_manifest.ps1 documents that non-FailClosed read failures return fallback state.
No test injects a manifest change/failure between discovery and phase sorting.
existing_safeguards: Initial discovery read is fail closed
entry priority levels are retained
strategy sort is deterministic for a given manifest
safeguard_gap: The two stages can observe different manifest versions and only the second read is allowed to fail open.
tests_present: PowerShell priority-manifest and queue-strategy checks cover stable manifests
tests_missing: Manifest corruption/change between discovery and phase plan
one immutable manifest version drives bucket and sort metadata
recommended_remediation: Pass the validated manifest or canonical immutable ordering metadata into phase planning, bind its hash/version into the queue fingerprint, and remove the non-fail-closed re-read.
remediation_risk: medium: concurrency and legacy callers need careful coordination; preserve deterministic sorting and existing strategy semantics
validation_rung: PowerShell deterministic concurrency fixture around discovery/phase planning, priority strategy tests, and Python queue preview/launch fingerprint tests; real media is not required.

title: Saving a schedule over corrupt app state silently erases unrelated machine and authentication state
observed_behavior: load_app_state catches parse/read failure and returns ordinary defaults, so the facade receives no warning. A confirmed schedule change then calls save_app_state with only schedule keys; its load-merge catches the same failure, replaces existing state with an empty mapping, and atomically overwrites the file. Unrelated keys explicitly named in the contract, including machine_id and coordinator_auth_token, are lost.
expected_invariant: A partial app-state save must never overwrite an existing but unreadable state file or discard unrelated identity, credential, and UI keys. Corrupt authority must block mutation or be preserved for explicit recovery.
root_cause: Both read layers collapse existing-unreadable state into default/empty state; the warning is only logged and is not returned to the command contract or used to prevent overwrite.
failure_scenario: app_state.json is truncated by external storage failure. The operator opens Schedule, sees defaults without a read warning, confirms a schedule edit, and the backend replaces the file with schedule-only state. Machine identity, coordinator authentication token, and preferences can no longer be recovered from the original bytes.
evidence: app_state.py lines 41-45 returns defaults after any read exception.
app_state.py lines 65-71 substitutes an empty merge base after any existing-file read exception.
facade.py lines 39-58 can report read warnings only if the service raises, but the service swallows the exception.
facade.py line 145 saves only schedule_enabled and schedule_grid.

A temporary current-code probe starting from malformed JSON produced a valid schedule payload with machine_id and coordinator_auth_token absent; existing tests only prove preservation from valid JSON.
existing_safeguards: Strict confirm_save is required
writes are atomic
valid existing extra keys are load-merged and preserved
read failures are logged
safeguard_gap: Confirmation covers the schedule change, not silent destruction of unrelated unreadable authority, and logging neither warns the operator nor blocks overwrite.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_schedule.py verifies unrelated keys survive a save when app state is valid
tests_missing: Corrupt existing app state blocks schedule save without overwriting bytes

title: A running audit snapshot can be classified safe to close when pipeline progress is empty
observed_behavior: get_close_readiness reduces the supplied snapshot to one state and does not independently preserve its active audit evidence. The shared reducer returns idle as soon as pipeline CurrentStage is empty, before inspecting snapshot.audit_progress. If the separate persisted audit re-read is absent or stale, close readiness reports safe_to_close=True for a snapshot whose audit status is running.
expected_invariant: Any current backend-authored snapshot that proves an audit is running must block native shell close, regardless of whether pipeline progress is empty or a separate persistence re-read has aged out.
root_cause: The facade trusts a lossy combined state reducer and passes no snapshot-level audit blocker into close_readiness_fields; empty pipeline stage takes precedence over active audit progress in that reducer.
failure_scenario: An audit is active while the pipeline progress section is empty and the on-disk audit progress lookup returns no fresh row. The operator closes the shell, close readiness returns safe, and the active audit can be terminated without the mandated lifecycle warning/block.
evidence: guard_facade.py lines 132-142 supplies only the collapsed state plus independent durable block_message to close_readiness_fields.
Current application state reduction returns idle for an empty pipeline stage before its later audit-status branch.
The focused existing test constructs progress={} and audit_progress.status=running; current code returns safe_to_close=True.
The test failure reproduced both in the 111-test focused rung and alone: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_close_readiness.py:115.
existing_safeguards: Fresh persisted audit progress blocks close
known active combined states block close
missing snapshots and unverified process state fail closed
safeguard_gap: The snapshot already contains authoritative active-audit evidence, but the facade discards it before applying the close policy and relies on a second state source that may be absent.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_close_readiness.py explicitly expects a running audit snapshot to block close
tests_missing: Regression coverage for empty pipeline progress plus active audit that currently passes in CI
recommended_remediation: Make snapshot audit activity an explicit fail-closed input to close readiness or change the combined reducer to evaluate active audit before returning an idle pipeline state; retain the durable re-read as corroborating recovery evidence.
remediation_risk: low-medium: state precedence changes can conservatively block close on stale audit snapshots, so freshness/source authority should remain explicit
validation_rung: Fix and rerun the focused close-readiness suite, Local API lifecycle contract tests, and Tauri close adversarial tests; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed by an existing currently failing regression test; no current finding fragment described this snapshot-audit state-precedence defect.
